_comment: What each fixture in this directory is. Everything here is the TARGET shape from docs/tasks/refactor/API-CONTRACT-v1.md. None of it is what the API returns today -- see ../shipped/ for that, and ../../README.md for which of the differences are blocked rather than merely unbuilt. Nothing in this directory is verified by frontend/verify_fixtures.py, deliberately: there is no code to verify it against.
_status: TARGET. Build the client against these; expect the shipped shapes at runtime until tasks 28, 30 and 32 land.
_status_correction_2026_08_02: 28 and 32 have landed and 25 landed alongside them, so 'the shipped shapes' are now the only shapes a client sees for everything except `bucket` and `tracks[]`, which remain task 30's and remain blocked. Three files in this directory describe an endpoint that ships and describes it WRONGLY -- the three ASPIRATIONAL_*searches* ones -- and their differences are enumerated in _searches_deviations rather than resolved. Do not build a parser against them; ../shipped/ has eleven files for the same feature.

_endpoint_reality.POST /v1/events: route exists (jobs.py:641), request shape agrees, response is undocumented in the contract
_endpoint_reality.GET /v1/me: route exists (auth.py:450); the onboarding block is aspirational
_endpoint_reality.GET /v1/searches: WAS 'NO ROUTE, NO TABLE … re-grepped 2026-08-02, still zero hits across backend/' AND THAT WENT FALSE IN e3abd6e, ON THE DAY IT WAS RE-GREPPED. Task 25 landed four tables (search_queries, search_query_watchers, search_query_signal, search_query_results) and six routes in backend/webapp/search.py. This one and the four below it are real. Shape differs -- see _searches_deviations.
_endpoint_reality.POST /v1/searches: ROUTE AND TABLE, same commit. Shape differs -- see _searches_deviations.
_endpoint_reality.GET /v1/searches/{id}: ROUTE, and it is not in API-CONTRACT-v1.md at all. ../shipped/GET_v1_searches_by_id.json.
_endpoint_reality.POST /v1/searches/{id}/unwatch: ROUTE, not in the contract. A POST rather than a DELETE because app.py's CORS middleware allows GET, POST and OPTIONS only.
_endpoint_reality.GET /v1/searches/{id}/results: ROUTE, not in the contract, and the one that carries the postings. Returns /v1/jobs' shape field for field. ../shipped/GET_v1_searches_results.json.
_endpoint_reality.POST /v1/onboarding: MOVED TO ../shipped/ ON 2026-08-02. It has a route (onboarding.py) and builder_profiles is a real table (schema_web.py), so the two ASPIRATIONAL_POST_v1_onboarding.* files that used to live here are now shipped/POST_v1_onboarding.{request,response}.json and are checked by verify_fixtures.py. One deviation was found on the way and the FIXTURE was wrong: completed_at carried a trailing 'Z' this endpoint never sends.
_endpoint_reality.GET /v1/onboarding: HAS A ROUTE AND IS NOT IN THE CONTRACT AT ALL. See ../shipped/GET_v1_onboarding.json. The contract covers reading onboarding state with an invented block on GET /v1/me (ASPIRATIONAL_GET_v1_me.json, edge-cases/06); the code answers it with its own route instead, and onboarding.py says why. The two must never both exist with different shapes.

GET_v1_jobs.json.shows: tracks[] grouping, bucket, nested comp{}/why{}/state{}, posting_age_days, cohort_signal, apply_url, and NO raw match_score or fit_score.
notes: rank is global across the render, not per-track. The ranks here are 1,3 / 2 / 4 -- deliberately interleaved across tracks, because that is what 'the ordering the user actually saw' means. A client that renumbers within a track has broken the position-bias instrumentation.

TRACK VOCABULARY IS THE ONE OPEN QUESTION IN THIS DIRECTORY. The contract's single example is `ai_operations`, which is a role_archetype value in config/pursuit-criteria.json, not a track. The only track vocabulary that exists in the code is score.TRACKS (score.py:281-282): 'Core SWE', 'AI Integration', 'Bridge & Solutions', 'Re-Entry & Growth', 'Poor Fit'. These fixtures slugify those, and put the stored Title Case form in `label`. Whoever implements task 32 has to decide this; it is recorded here rather than resolved.
'Poor Fit' is a real score.TRACKS value and is deliberately absent from every fixture. Whether it is ever rendered is a product decision nobody has made.

GET_v1_jobs_by_id.json.shows: the same job object plus description_html, source{}, closes_at and facts{}.
notes: closes_at has no column anywhere in schema.py. It is not merely unimplemented; there is nothing to read it from.

description_html is a different thing from the shipped description_text, which is plain text. Somebody has to decide where the HTML comes from -- the ATS payload keeps it, the pipeline does not store it.
source.first_seen is a date here; the shipped first_seen is a full '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S' stamp.

POST_v1_events.request.json.shows: all seven client event names in one batch, including undismiss and applied.
notes: This body is VALID against the shipped validator today -- it is the one place the contract and the code already agree, after DEC-73 moved the contract from `apply` to `applied`.
undismiss carries no rank and no reason; a reason here is a 400 with code reason_not_allowed (jobs.py:514-519).

POST_v1_events.response.json.shows: the shipped {recorded, deduped, skipped, derived_skips} response.
notes: The contract specifies no response body for this endpoint. This fixture is the shipped shape, carried into the contract set so a client has something to type against.

ASPIRATIONAL_GET_v1_me.json.shows: the shipped four keys plus an onboarding block.
notes: The onboarding block is invented. The contract has POST /v1/onboarding and no way to READ onboarding state, and a first-run client needs one. See edge-cases/06.

_searches_deviations._comment: WHAT THE CONTRACT ASKED FOR AND WHAT SHIPPED, recorded 2026-08-02 by task 32's stream on building the search screen against the real routes. These three files STAY here rather than moving to ../shipped/ -- unlike the two onboarding fixtures, which moved because the shape they described turned out to be the shape that shipped. These describe a shape that was never built, and the difference is the artifact. The shipped API was NOT changed to match them.
_searches_deviations.1_watcher_count_vs_watcher_bucket: ASPIRATIONAL_GET_v1_searches.json exposes `watcher_count: 7` and `watcher_count: 1`. The shipped field is `watcher_bucket`, which is a LABEL ('4-6' / '7-10' / '11+') or null, and null covers 0, 1, 2 and 3 indistinguishably because search_query_signal holds no row below schema.SEARCH_MIN_WATCHERS = 4. THE CONTRACT'S OWN FIXTURE CONTAINS THE THING THE SUPPRESSION EXISTS TO PREVENT: `watcher_count: 1` on query 51 is one identifiable person, in a thirty-person cohort who sit in a room together, on a query anyone can create by typing it. DEC-85 sets out why the floor is 4 here where cohort_signal's is 3 -- the observed object is attacker-chosen and the planter is always a watcher -- and DEC-87 why the count is a separate table rather than a column the service could write. This is the one deviation where the contract is not merely unbuilt but wrong, and it must not be 'fixed' towards the fixture.
_searches_deviations.2_one_nested_response_vs_two_scoped_requ: The contract returns ONE body nesting {suggested, mine}. The shipped route returns {searches, scope} and takes a `scope` parameter, so a client that wants both makes two requests -- js/search.mjs issues them together with Promise.all. Two consequences worth stating: the two scopes OVERLAP (a seeded query the caller watches is in both, byte for byte), which a nested shape would have hidden; and there is deliberately no third scope, because the TEXT of a builder-created query is often self-identifying and a browsable list of everyone's would hand an observer the whole population to plant against.
_searches_deviations.3_202_with_a_queue_position_vs_200_with_: ASPIRATIONAL_POST_v1_searches.response.json is a 202 carrying `status: 'queued'`, `queue_position: 4` and `estimated_ready_at`. The shipped route answers 200 with the query object. None of the three invented fields has a column and nothing computes a queue depth: searchqueries.py picks up whatever is due on the nightly cycle, so there is no position in a queue to report. The shipped answer to 'when will this run' is `last_run_at` being null, which the client renders as "This one hasn't run yet". Honest, and cheaper than a number that would have to be made up.
_searches_deviations.4_the_request_carries_no_watching_flag: ASPIRATIONAL_POST_v1_searches.request.json sends `watching: true`. SearchRequest has three fields -- text, location, chips -- and no such flag, and it could not have one: the submitter is registered as a watcher unconditionally, which is what makes tranche_four/25's 'a query submitted by two Builders creates one row with two watchers' true. A flag would make it optional and the cost argument would stop holding.
_searches_deviations.5_the_contract_covers_two_of_six_routes: It has GET and POST /v1/searches and nothing else. GET /v1/searches/{id}, the watch/unwatch pair and GET /v1/searches/{id}/results are all shipped and all absent from API-CONTRACT-v1.md -- and the last of those is the one that actually carries postings, so the contract as written describes a search feature with no way to read a result.

ASPIRATIONAL_GET_v1_searches.json.shows: suggested[] and mine[], verbatim from API-CONTRACT-v1.md § GET /v1/searches.
notes: ~~watcher_count is exposed; watcher identities never are. No route, no table, task 25.~~ THE ROUTE AND THE TABLES EXIST as of e3abd6e; see _endpoint_reality above and ../shipped/GET_v1_searches.{suggested,mine}.json.

The struck sentence was also wrong in a way worth keeping: exposing a raw `watcher_count` is not 'identities never are'. A count of one IS close to an identity here, which is the whole of _searches_deviations item 1.
Request shape is inferred; the contract shows only the GET response.
The inference was wrong in one field and right in two: `watching` does not exist and cannot (_searches_deviations item 4), and there is no `chips` here, which the shipped model does have.
202 with a queue position, per the contract. Searches are asynchronous -- never block a Builder on a scrape; results appear on the next list.

THE ASYNCHRONY IS RIGHT AND THE SHAPE IS NOT. Shipped is 200 with the query object, whose null `last_run_at` says the same thing without inventing a queue nobody measures. _searches_deviations item 3.

errors/error_envelope.json.shows: the contract's envelope, which IS shipped for ContractError (jobs.py:151-157).
notes: It is not shipped for 401/403/404/malformed-cursor. See ../shipped/errors/NOT-ENVELOPED-*.json.

edge-cases/._comment: The six states API-CONTRACT-v1.md § Mocking names as 'the states most likely to be skipped'. All six are in contract shape.
edge-cases/.01-track-with-zero-jobs.json: Two tracks with empty jobs[]. A track is not omitted when it is empty -- the blurb still has to render, or the list silently shrinks and nobody can tell whether the track was filtered or was empty.
edge-cases/.02-job-with-null-comp.json: comp is null outright, not an object of nulls. Distinguishing 'no salary stated' from 'salary of zero' is the whole point.
edge-cases/.03-comp-is-estimated.json: comp.is_estimated true. Adzuna predicts salary; showing a prediction as though the employer stated it is a trust problem, not a formatting one (contract, task 35).
edge-cases/.04-cohort-signal-null.json: cohort_signal null, which is what fewer than three saves looks like. Never an exact count, never a recency, never an identity -- the suppression is a privacy control, enforced server-side (task 28).
edge-cases/.05-empty-mine-search-list.json: mine is [] while suggested is populated. GET /v1/searches shape; aspirational in its NESTING but the state itself is real and is now frozen as ../../shipped/GET_v1_searches.mine.empty.json. It is the state every Builder starts in, and the reason the client renders the seeded catalogue above 'Your searches' rather than beside it.
edge-cases/.06-first-run-user-no-onboarding.json: onboarding.completed false with prior_domain NULL. NULL is not the same as the domain literally named 'none': schema_web.py:136-141 makes that distinction load-bearing -- 'none' is a real answer about a real person, NULL means nobody asked. A first-run user is NULL.
